Some years ago- maybe 10 by now- Dad had his leg amputated due to a diabetes-related blood clot. He managed his diet well and was borderline-obsessive about his blood sugar level, but shit happens sometimes. As one might expect, depression set in for awhile. The doctors tried to save as much of the leg as possible, amputating below the knee so that he could have a simpler prosthetic leg that would be easier to use. That didn't work, so he had to go back and have another amputation, above the knee. That didn't help his depression. Again- as one might expect.

He now calls it the best thing that's ever happened to him. If that clot had gone up instead of down, he could have had a heart attack or a stroke. He could have been killed or become a vegetable. Instead, he got to live- which he started doing. He started up with hobbies that he'd long abandoned. He started becoming more active in his community. He even got a wicked sense of humor about it. Started carrying a sword cane on occasion. Not that he had a use for the sword, but it was funny. He hadn't told his dietitian about his leg, so at his next appointment he stepped on the scale and showed a significant weight loss. He let the poor nurse twist in the wind awhile, trying to figure out what in his diet and exercise was causing such a rapid weight loss, and then dropped an "Oh, yeah- it might be this" and showed her the titanium leg.
